explain: _patriae_ is the genitive of _patria_ (homeland): it says what the love is directed at, “love of country”.
distractors: _patriam_ is accusative. A noun after _amor_ names what it is love of: genitive, _patriae_.
_patriārum_ is genitive plural (“of homelands”). You love one country: _patriae_.

explain: _mortis_ is the genitive of _mors_ (death): it says what the fear is directed at.
distractors: _mortium_ is genitive plural (“of deaths”). Death here is one thing: _mortis_.

en: Fear of the enemies is great.
explain: _metus_ is fourth declension (nominative _metus_). _hostium_ is the genitive plural of _hostis_: it says whom the fear is of.
distractors: _hostibus_ is dative or ablative plural. After _metus_: genitive, _hostium_.
_hostis_ here would be genitive singular: “fear of one enemy”. For “the enemies”, use _hostium_.

explain: _spēs_ is fifth declension (feminine, so _magna_). _victōriae_ is the genitive of _victōria_: what the hope is of.
distractors: _victōriārum_ is genitive plural. One hope, one victory: _victōriae_.

en: The boy is eager for glory.
explain: _cupidus_ (eager, desirous) is followed by the genitive of what you want: _glōriae_.
distractors: _glōriārum_ is genitive plural. Glory as a mass is singular: _glōriae_.

en: The man is greedy for money.
explain: _avidus_ (greedy, eager) takes the genitive: _pecūniae_ says what he is greedy for.
distractors: _pecūniārum_ is genitive plural. Money as a mass is singular: _pecūniae_.

en: The house is full of books.
explain: _plēna_ (full) agrees with feminine _domus_; what it is full of goes in the genitive: _librōrum_ (genitive plural of _liber_).
distractors: _librī_ is genitive singular (“of a book”). Many books: _librōrum_.
_plēnus_ is masculine, but _domus_ is feminine here. The adjective agrees: _plēna_.

en: The man is experienced in war.
explain: _perītus_ (experienced, skilled) takes the genitive of what you are skilled in: _bellī_ (of war).
distractors: _bella_ is plural (“wars”). One kind of skill: the genitive singular _bellī_.
_bellōrum_ is genitive plural (“of wars”). Say _bellī_ for skill in war.

en: I am not greedy for money.
explain: A man says _cupidus_ of himself, so it is masculine: “I am (a man) desirous of money”. The genitive _pecūniae_ is what he wants.
distractors: _pecūniārum_ is genitive plural. Money as a mass is singular: _pecūniae_.

explain: _speī_ is the genitive singular of _spēs_ (fifth declension, genitive _-eī_). After _plēnus_ the thing you are full of is genitive.
distractors: _spēs_ is nominative (or accusative plural). After _plēnus_: genitive, _speī_.
